content.title: What is JDBC?
content.description: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) is a standard Java API that enables Java applications to connect to relational databases, execute SQL queries, and process the results.

content.content: JDBC (Java Database Connectivity) acts as a bridge between Java applications and relational databases such as MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, and SQL Server. It allows developers to establish database connections, execute SQL statements, retrieve query results, and perform CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) operations.

content.title: Why JDBC?
content.content: JDBC provides a standard way for Java applications to communicate with different relational databases using SQL, making database operations portable and efficient.
JDBC Components
The JDBC API consists of several important classes and interfaces that work together to communicate with a database.

content.title: Key Idea
content.description: JDBC provides a database-independent API. Only the JDBC driver changes when connecting to different databases.

content.content: JDBC Workflow
A typical JDBC program follows a series of steps to establish a connection, execute SQL statements, and retrieve results.
Establishing a Connection
The DriverManager class is commonly used to establish a connection between the Java application and the database.
Executing SQL Queries
Once connected, SQL queries can be executed using Statement or PreparedStatement objects.

content.title: Statement Example
content.code:
Statement stmt = con.createStatement();
ResultSet rs = stmt.executeQuery("SELECT * FROM students");

content.content: Reading Query Results
The ResultSet object stores rows returned by a SELECT query and allows iteration through each record.

content.content: Real-Life Analogy

content.title: Restaurant Waiter
content.content: Think of JDBC as a waiter in a restaurant. The customer (Java application) places an order (SQL query), the waiter (JDBC) communicates with the kitchen (database), and finally delivers the prepared food (query result) back to the customer.

content.title: Interview Importance
content.content: JDBC architecture, DriverManager, Connection, Statement, PreparedStatement, ResultSet, JDBC driver types, SQL Injection prevention, transactions, and CRUD operations are among the most frequently asked Java interview topics.
Common Mistakes

items.question: Why should PreparedStatement be preferred over Statement?
items.answer: PreparedStatement prevents SQL Injection attacks and improves performance for repeated queries.

items.question: Why should JDBC resources be closed?
items.answer: Leaving connections, statements, or result sets open can lead to memory leaks and resource exhaustion.

items.question: Is loading the JDBC driver always required manually?
items.answer: No. Modern JDBC drivers support automatic driver loading, although older versions required Class.forName().

The JDBC workflow includes connecting, executing queries, processing results, and closing resources.
